pressable rather than glassy. Headings and plant names use a local serif
(Georgia/Iowan stack) against a rounded humanist body stack — no web fonts, no
network. The shape language is deliberately lopsided: organic asymmetric
border-radii on cards and panels, leaf-shaped progress dots and timeline
bullets, blob-shaped portrait wells.

The oddness lives in the details: every plant has a hand-built inline SVG
portrait with its own silhouette (arching fern fronds, a trailing heart-leaf
vine, bunny-ear pads with a tiny flower, striped orbifolia discs), foliage
sways when a card is hovered or focused, the all-done state is a smiling sun
over three contented pots, and the copy talks like a friend ("Frida has been
waiting 2 days and goes first. The rest can bask.", "Drama folds her leaves at
dusk like a fainting couch. This is normal, really."). Delight moments are
small and brief: water drops fall over a card when it is watered, cards poof
out when snoozed, bars grow from the soil line once on load.

## Interaction model

- **One queue, honest priority.** The four plants from `PLANTS.json` (embedded
  verbatim in `app.js` so the page makes zero requests and also works from
  `file://`) are sorted by `urgency`, so overdue care always leads. Overdue
  cards get a terracotta spine, tinted wash and a pulsing dot in the due badge;
  today/tomorrow get calmer badges. The lede sentence and the leaf-dot progress
  meter restate the situation in plain words.
- **Expand, don't navigate.** "Details" is a disclosure button on each card
  (`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`) opening an inline panel with location,
  light, a watering rule, a one-line quirk note, and the observation history as
  an icon-coded timeline (drop, mist, rotate, sprout, sparkle, eye). Escape
  closes the open panel and returns focus to its toggle.
- **Actions with a way back.** The primary button is task-specific ("Watered",
  "Rotated", "Soil checked", "Misted"); "Snooze" parks a plant in a dashed
  "Snoozing until tomorrow" zone with a Wake button. Every mutation raises a
  toast with an Undo button (7s), and completed plants keep a persistent Undo
  in the "Tended today" panel, so the undo path survives the toast.
- **Endings.** When the queue empties, a calm celebration panel appears with
  three wordings (all tended / mixed with snoozes / everything snoozed) plus a
  "Start the day over" reset, so the state is useful rather than a dead end.
- **Weekly rhythm.** The `week` array renders as seven sprout-topped bars over
  a soil strip; today's bar is terracotta and underlined, and the caption names
  the busiest day.

## Desktop composition

Above 940px the page becomes a two-column grid instead of a stretched phone:
the queue keeps a readable measure on the left while a sticky right rail holds
the rhythm chart, the "Tended today" ledger and a "Small wisdom" note, so
status information is visible without scrolling away from the queue.

## Accessibility choices

- Semantic structure: `header/main/aside/footer`, one `h1`, sectioned `h2`s,
  the queue is an ordered list of cards, all controls are real `<button>`s with
  task- and plant-specific accessible names ("Watered — complete Frida's water
  task", "Snooze Dot until tomorrow").
- Keyboard: skip link to the queue, visible 3px focus rings via
  `:focus-visible`, ArrowUp/Down/Home/End rove between matching controls across
  cards, Escape collapses the open detail panel, and focus is moved
  deliberately after an action (next card's primary button, or the all-done
  panel) so removal never strands the cursor.
- Live feedback without noise: the toast is a single `role="status"` region; a
  separate visually-hidden status line announces progress ("2 of 4 plants
  tended today…") and detail-panel openings.
- The rhythm chart is `aria-hidden` visually but mirrored by a hidden
  sentence listing every day's count and marking today.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` collapses all animation and transition
  durations in CSS, and JavaScript checks the same media query to skip the
  water-drop burst and exit animations entirely, swapping state instantly.
- Contrast: body ink on cream and button fills were chosen to stay above WCAG
  AA; badges pair tinted backgrounds with dark ink rather than relying on hue.
